messages:
tess: FYI the new ESM-first SDK change made our edge quickstart fail in CI. tsc complains about duplicate ambient types and an odd generic inference where T becomes unknown.

noah: can you paste the error + the tsconfig used for the edge bundle?

ci-bot:
```
> tsc -p tsconfig.edge.json
src/sdk/edge.ts:58:22 - error TS2345: Argument of type 'T' is not assignable to parameter of type 'unknown'.
58   return edgeClient.request<T>(route, body)
                        ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
src/types/global.d.ts:12:5 - error TS2300: Duplicate identifier 'EdgeOptions'.
12 export interface EdgeOptions { timeout?: number }
```

kai: Two things to check: 1) are we including "node" in types for the edge tsconfig? 2) are we emitting declarations for the edge artifacts? Emitting .d.ts plus bundling can duplicate declarations.

tess: tsconfig.edge.json had {"moduleResolution":"bundler","lib":["DOM","ES2021"],"types":["node"],"declaration":true}. We use esbuild to produce the edge bundle.

noah: simplest fix: for the edge pipeline set "types": [] (or explicitly ["web"]), set "declaration": false, and add "skipLibCheck": true. Also ensure package.exports doesn't accidentally route edge imports to cjs/node runtime.

kai: separate but related: we had an overloaded runtime.request signatures that confused inference. Example: 
```
export function request<T>(path: string, body: T): Promise<R<T>>
export function request(path: string, body: unknown): Promise<R<unknown>>
export function request(path: string, body: any) { /* impl */ }
```
Calling request('p', {x:1}) sometimes resolves to any/unknown depending on overload order.

tess: ugh. Is that a TS bug?

kai: it's how overload resolution + generics interact. Workarounds: - put the non-generic overloads first and generic last, - provide a thin generic wrapper helper like `export const requestTyped = <T>(p: string, b: T) => request<T>(p, b)`, or - encourage users to call with explicit generic when inference matters.

noah: also add an examples/edge-typed sample in the repo showing recommended tsconfig, bundler flags, and the wrapper. Document the unknown vs any guidance: public API surfaces should use unknown to force narrowing, but we provide typed helpers so consumers get good inference.

tess: I changed tsconfig.edge.json to {"compilerOptions":{"lib":["DOM","ES2021"],"types":[],"moduleResolution":"bundler","skipLibCheck":true,"declaration":false}} and CI built fine locally.

kai: I'll open a PR to add an edge/README.md with the tsconfig and a Vite/esbuild sample config plus a short note on export maps. Also add a test that builds the edge bundle to ensure we don't accidentally ship node types.

noah: good call. small lint rule idea: detect if tsconfig for edge has node types or declaration=true and warn in CI.

tess: thanks, will follow up in the PR. closing once CI green on the branch.
